sentence: This project uses real-world data and physiological sensing to study dysgeusia and to guide nutrition for people with taste loss.
This project plans and reviews the work of a cancer center that aims to find cures for pediatric cancer.
This project tries to find out why the spine stiffens too early after surgery with growing rods in children with early onset scoliosis.
This project builds statistical tools that measure how uncertain results are when studying communities of microorganisms from sequencing data.
This project studies how partner proteins interact with dynamin-related protein 1 to control mitochondrial division.
This project uses deep learning on echocardiography images to find features of mitral valve disease that may point to ways to lower cardiovascular risk.
This project uses tools that find non-coding variants and DNA-protein interactions to explain how genetic risk leads to juvenile idiopathic arthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.
This project studies how cell signaling, protein stability, and gene regulation control a cancer gene that promotes tumor growth in some cancers.
This project develops a head and neck cancer treatment that uses membrane vesicles from a patient's own tumor and an immune checkpoint inhibitor.
This project uses experimental evolution in yeast to find genes and pathways that respond to selective pressures.
This project builds nanopore tweezers that study the motions of kinase proteins to help with drug design and screening for cancer therapeutics.
This project tries to find out how thiol reductive stress stops tumor growth and metastasis in lung cancer by blocking mitochondrial respiration.
This project looks for modifier genes that affect the age-of-onset and severity of Alport syndrome, a kidney disease, in mouse and human.
This project improves a DNA recording tool that lets living cells write down when genes turn on and off during development.
This project brings together cancer research, epidemiology, biostatistics, genetics, and computer science to study cancer genetics and genomics.
This project studies which molecular changes during development are shared among primate species and which are found only in humans.
This project studies how cell mechanics, controlled by a noncoding RNA, drive hair follicle stem cell division and hair growth in young and geriatric mice.
This project builds tools that combine lipid nanodiscs and mass spectrometry to study how membrane proteins interact with the lipids around them.
This project tests the safety and immune response of a preventive tau vaccine in people who are cognitively unimpaired and preclinical.
This project uses metabolomics and machine learning to find metabolite biomarkers of neurocognitive impairment in older people with HIV.
